source.snippet: I had the misfortune of China Eastern Airlines losing my luggage. It's been several months now, with no more hope of finding it. My fiancée's jewellery box was inside, and I can provide at least €2,000 of invoices for the contents (the 7000 is total value, 2000 is what I can prove with receipts). However, China Eastern is only offering €300 in compensation. And AirAdvisor didn't help at all — not one bit. It was a flight from Japan to Paris with a connection in Shanghai. What can I do to ramp up the pressure?

problem_statement: Airline passengers who suffer lost luggage with high-value contents receive lowball compensation offers (e.g. €300 against €2,000+ in documented losses) and existing claim services like AirAdvisor fail to escalate effectively, leaving passengers without recourse guidance for international itineraries.
target_segment: Frequent travelers and business travelers who have experienced lost or damaged luggage on international flights, particularly involving non-EU carriers
notes: Buyer signal moderate: the poster has €2,000+ in documented losses and already tried a paid/service-based solution (AirAdvisor) that failed. Willingness to pay for effective claim assistance is implied by the stakes. However, this is a single signal and the space has existing players (AirAdvisor, AirHelp). Opportunity may be in specialization: non-EU carriers (China Eastern, etc.) where Montreal Convention claims are harder to navigate, or a done-for-you documentation and escalation service. Lower signal strength due to single data point and existing competition.
